paper_title: Limits on new long-range nuclear spin-dependent forces set with a K-3He co-magnetometer
notes: Solid curve ('this work', derivative coupling) from Fig. 4, extracted from the vector EPS (axionlimitMore_g2.eps -> PDF, pymupdf get_drawings, fill region idx7 lower boundary). This is a dipole-dipole (spin-spin) search between neutrons via a pseudoscalar boson; the plotted y-axis is (g_p^n)^2/(4pi). The paper's pseudoscalar coupling is defined via L^Der = (g_p/2M_n) psibar gamma_mu gamma5 psi d^mu phi (Eq. 2), which is identical to the canonical g_an normalisation L=(g_an/2m_n) d_mu a nbar gamma^mu gamma5 n, so g_p^n = g_an directly (no 2m_N factor needed; the 2M_n is already in the paper's Lagrangian). Converted g_an = sqrt(4pi * [(g_p^n)^2/4pi]). Flat massless-boson value (g_p^n)^2/4pi < 5.8e-10 (quoted, 1sigma) -> g_an < 8.54e-5; calibration verified against this value (y=403.5px). x-axis m in meV converted to eV (x1e-3). Curve is flat for m below ~1e-7 eV then rises steeply near m~1e-6 eV (10^-3 meV) as the Yukawa/r^3 exchange is suppressed beyond the ~48.7 cm source-detector range. Paper states a 1sigma (68% CL) limit, so confidence_level=0.68 (not 0.90/0.95). This constrains the neutron coupling with the source also being a neutron spin (^3He), i.e. g_an^2; reported as the single canonical g_an.
